# The nickname syntax, one case a line: kind TAB input TAB canonical key.
# Read by the Go tests (nickbot/internal/nick) and by the C++ core tests (tests/bmclient/nickbot_test.cpp):
# the two implementations must agree on every line. "ok" lines have a key, "no" lines have none.
# A person (@) and a bot (/) are case-insensitive: their key is lower case. A chan (#) is a passphrase and
# keeps its case. The name is 3 to 32 characters, the first a letter, the rest letters, digits, _ and -.
ok	@ben	@ben
ok	@Ben	@ben
ok	@BEN	@ben
ok	/echobot	/echobot
ok	/EchoBot	/echobot
ok	#general	#general
ok	#General	#General
ok	@a_b-c	@a_b-c
ok	@b2b	@b2b
ok	@abc	@abc
ok	@Quick_Otter_Of_Zeta	@quick_otter_of_zeta
ok	@abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdef	@abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdef
ok	@ben_	@ben_
ok	@ben-	@ben-
ok	@a--b	@a--b
ok	#My-Chan_1	#My-Chan_1
no	@abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdefg
no	@be
no	@b
no	@
no	/
no	#
no	ben
no	ben@
no	@@ben
no	@/ben
no	!ben
no	$ben
no	@1ben
no	@_ben
no	@-ben
no	@ben bob
